items_missed: Never got or confirmed the customer's name — she used his name repeatedly, he never used hers once
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation before diving into the inventory review
Never verified origin or destination address/zip — he re-verified floors and walk distance but not the addresses themselves
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops
Never asked the moving-stressor question — the customer's actual stressor (two wildly different quotes) surfaced only because she raised it
Never stated the hourly rate himself; when she said 'it's just the 218' he let it pass without confirming
Customer literally asked 'so everything is included' and he redirected to packing instead of running the what's-included list (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools)
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — and she asked directly how the mattress would be protected, which is the natural bridge into it
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — the customer's opening question was literally about the arrival window, the single best setup for it in any of this week's calls
No 'no hidden fees' pitch and no 'pricing is super simple' opener
Entire Clock section skipped — never said the clock starts on-site, never confirmed the 2.5-hour minimum when she raised it, never explained 15-minute prorated increments, no sense-check
Never stated the number of movers and trucks anywhere in the call
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped, despite the customer packing all fifteen boxes herself
No bolded-details list or 'reply with any corrections' when describing the move confirmation email
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' — the close was three overlapping goodbyes
top_strength: Best estimate work of the three calls. He rebuilt the inventory line by line, caught that the file said first floor when she is actually on the fourth, pressure-tested the 50-foot walk at both ends, and then talked the 7-hour quote down to roughly six with his reasoning shown ('elevators do tend to push this over our typical range of three and a half to six and a half'). He also committed to calling Dustin to reconcile the two quotes rather than just overriding a colleague.
coaching_note: He won this customer on credibility and then left the entire value story on the table — no clock explanation, no included-list, no No Worries coverage, and no On-Time Guarantee even though her opening question was about arrival windows. When a customer is comparison-shopping and asks 'so everything is included?', that is the cue to run the full pricing and differentiator block, not a one-word answer.
phone_presence_notes: Knowledgeable, credible, and consultative, but transactional in language — no name use, no affirmations or empathy markers, and a clipped overlapping close, even though the customer ended enthusiastic ('Amazing! Thank you guys so much').
